resources.text:
SYNTHETIC RESEARCH NOTEBOOK · Celestial materials

Question
How can an immense orbital structure establish scale without competing with ordinary reading? These observations are invented review material, not measurements or published research.

01 / Cross section before ornament
A broad structural shell should have a visible inner face, a narrower recessed band, and a controlled outer lip. Repeated ribs can reveal curvature and thickness, but repetition alone does not establish size. The silhouette extending beyond the viewport supplies the primary scale cue. Light should vary across the cross section rather than tracing the entire outline.

02 / A shared light field
The same pale violet direction should inform Vela’s pearl response and the architectural shell. A research lens may carry a cooler edge than a notebook, while the focused conversation uses a nearly opaque working plane. These are material roles within one environment. They do not require literal refraction or a costly transparent layer behind every paragraph.

03 / Motion with a cause
An idle field continues its own slow motion. A moving resource displaces a local footprint according to its actual position, and that influence settles after the gesture. A wide folio can have a broader footprint than the notebook. The disturbance should remain spatially bounded. Reduced motion keeps the final spatial relationship without requiring a ripple.

04 / Experiment ledger
A — Monumental ring: inspect partial visibility, continuous curvature, and selective support divisions.
B — Celestial aperture: inspect the space through layered shells, the relative depth of the opening, and the risk of a decorative halo.
C — Suspended observatory: inspect the relationship between a dominant structure and distant supporting forms. More objects are useful only if the hierarchy remains clear.

05 / Synthetic agent report
Source: material-review fixture. Reported status: comparison drafted. Verification: unavailable until actual output is reviewed. No external agent ran, no GPU benchmark is represented by this paragraph, and no owner approval is implied.

Review questions
Does the structure retain a dark, legible cross section in Efficient mode? Does the selected lens still feel like the same object after expansion? Can a paragraph be selected and copied without movement behind the text? Does a scene change preserve the draft, caret, and scroll position? Are the small labels readable at ordinary window sizes?

Working conclusion
Prefer one coherent architectural structure over a collection of luminous rings. Preserve the responsive field and the double-loop presence. Keep the reading face calm. These are fixture observations for a realistic reading workload, not the actual milestone evaluation.

SYNTHETIC WORKING DOCUMENT · Observatory review plan

Purpose
An intelligent observatory should make space for concentration. Architectural scale belongs to the surrounding environment; the document remains a stable, readable place to think. This fictional plan exercises long-form editing and navigation.

Work package 1 — Preserve continuity
Keep each resource’s canonical identity independent of its representation. Expanding the conversation must not create a second document. Returning to the workspace must preserve its draft and reading position. Switching between Living Intelligence and Luminous Architecture changes the environment around the same objects. An interrupted transition should reverse from its current pose and velocity.

Work package 2 — Review the compositions
Compare three actual rendered architectural studies. Examine the outer silhouette before looking for fine detail. An orbital shell should imply a larger structure beyond the window. The aperture should have convincing front-to-back separation. The suspended arrangement should keep a clear dominant form. Use the same window size for comparisons, and preserve a failed experiment when it teaches something useful.

Work package 3 — Evaluate focused work
Read the conversation’s coding discussion, then inspect the synthetic agent report. Distinguish a reported result from a checked event sequence. Select a sentence, scroll, edit this document, switch environments, and return. The environment should recede during these actions without disappearing abruptly. Vela should remain reachable without covering the text.

Task overview
Owner: fictional review team.
Dependencies: reproducible baseline, three comparable compositions, stable local drafts.
Proposed evidence: native screenshots, actual animation recording, functional regression checks, and bounded performance samples.
Open decisions: final artistic direction, sustained motion comfort, production host, and complete assistive-technology qualification.

Risk register
Excessive edge emission can flatten the shell into a neon line. Too many secondary forms can reduce the sense of scale. Transparent text surfaces can lower readability. Strong ambient motion may become distracting during a long session. Additional geometry can increase rendering cost without improving the image. Each concern needs direct observation rather than a claim based on implementation complexity.

Review notes
This is an editable synthetic document. Replace or extend any paragraph. Local changes stay in this dedicated prototype profile. No external AI or synchronization service is connected. A fixture’s narrative is not evidence of real work, measured performance, or artistic acceptance.
